quote: It's just replacing your current electric bill.
stewart_read: Rep explains the financial mechanism of solar payment replacement, which is closer-tier content that should be deferred to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be trying to quickly satisfy the objection to move the call forward rather than genuinely teaching product mechanics.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch line — 'that's exactly what our specialist walks through' — instead of explaining the payment swap directly.

quote: But it's gotta be a catch to it. What am I what am I eventually gonna pay?
stewart_read: This is a cost-skepticism objection that maps directly to the bill-flip trigger, but rep answers with qualification questions instead of flipping to 'what's expensive is staying with Excel.'
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deliberately delaying the flip until the bill number is captured, planning to flip later — but no flip ever occurs.
coaching_implication: Bank this line for the flip: 'What's actually costing you is what Xcel's already charging you every month.'

quote: How much is it ever how much something is gonna cost me something eventually?
stewart_read: Second occurrence of the same cost objection; rep again answers with feature/mechanism explanation rather than inverting.
coaching_implication: Recognize objection recurrence as a signal the flip hasn't landed — repeat the inversion, not the explanation.

quote: Let me just meet I don't wanna send you anything because I don't know who you are.
stewart_read: A trust/legitimacy objection surfaces mid-call because the intro never gave a strong legitimacy anchor (no mention of the lead source specifics beyond 'a form').
alternative_hypothesis: Rep did reference 'a form' at 00:08 which is a legitimacy anchor, so this may be residual general solar-scam anxiety rather than a pure intro failure.
coaching_implication: When resistance to sending personal info appears, re-anchor legitimacy explicitly (reference the specific form/date) rather than just pivoting to an easier ask.

quote: And oh, you know what? I go I'm I'm gonna go through surgery in a couple weeks.
stewart_read: Customer discloses upcoming hernia surgery as a trust gift while trying to work out scheduling; rep responds only with scheduling logistics, no acknowledgment of the health situation.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the disclosure as purely a scheduling constraint, not a vulnerability moment.
coaching_implication: A brief 'hope the surgery goes smoothly' acknowledgment before pivoting to date-picking would have built trust at near-zero cost.

stewart_read: Customer finally surfaces a usable kWh figure after nine minutes of struggle; rep just acknowledges the number and moves to next data point instead of reflecting it back as a forward-pulling hook.
coaching_implication: Use the number immediately: 'At 505 kWh a lot of homeowners in your area are seeing real savings — let's see what your design looks like.'

quote: Because I'm seeing here how much are you paying? Do you know? On average?
stewart_read: The dollar-amount bill ask comes extremely late (13:14) and gets only 'Too much' / 'I don't know' — the anchor is never actually captured in dollars.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the kWh screenshot as sufficient and treated the dollar question as a formality rather than the core anchor.
coaching_implication: Ask for the dollar bill amount in the first few minutes, before the kWh/screenshot slog, so it can be flipped early per bill_anchoring.capture_pattern.
